componentGuidance.ball: Shared ball design: an orange basketball at the preferred tilted three-quarter angle, with a clearly visible off-center seam crossing. Keep two main grooves crossing clearly and bowed side channels connecting at separate points; preserve a recognizable basketball junction instead of showing only parallel arcs. Dark-purple exterior outline, slightly narrower purple grooves and broad orange panels. Reuse for ordinary toy/sports balls while preserving intended count, size and spatial relations; keep specifically implied baseballs, beads, marbles, yarn balls and small jar counters appropriate to their own scene. Current v4 reference is accepted provisionally, with an unresolved seam/angle improvement. Do not treat its seams as a finished design standard; retain the improvement note when planning dependent artwork.
componentGuidance.mountain: Shared mountain design: purple slopes with white snow caps and dark-purple outlines. Preserve scene-specific features: ordinary mountains have closed summits, while an erupting volcano needs a visible open crater with connected plume and lava; snow may remain on unaffected flanks only. Keep Fuji's characteristic profile when Fuji is the subject.
componentGuidance.rice: Shared uncooked rice design: medium-small slender tapered ivory kernels, roughly 1/8 to 1/10 of the bag opening width in the still life, intermediate between the oversized v1 and tiny v2. Keep grains individually readable at quiz size with light economical detail, not thick purple outlines or peanut-like plump ovals. Do not apply the bag still life to a rice-paddy landscape.
componentGuidance.stone: Shared stone design: a slightly angular irregular gray silhouette with restrained mineral speckles, short cracks and a few broad natural planes. Avoid a smooth blob, symmetric gem facets or sparkles. Keep texture sparse enough to read at quiz size; scale this treatment for boulders.
componentGuidance.crowd-scope: For card69 / many, keep the jar rather than people. Crowds conflict with population and should remain available for that concept; do not reuse the rejected crowd as a many-card design reference.
